setting: You are all in the park in Mumbai, India, where you walk dogs for pay in the mornings and evenings. You have known each other for about a year through the same dog-walking group, seeing each other most days, and you know the basics of each other's work, dogs, and routines.
opener: Ask whether anyone can cover the 6pm walk, since you're stuck on a late delivery.

Rahul.knows: You know Kavita as an older dog walker who bakes and brings treats for the dogs, and Riya as a young architecture student who walks dogs part-time between classes.
Rahul.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly to swap shifts or say you're running late, rarely just to chat.

Kavita.knows: You know Rahul as a delivery rider who walks dogs with you on weekday evenings, and Riya as a young architecture student who joined the walks a few months ago.
Kavita.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly to share a bake or check who is coming to the morning walk.

Riya.knows: You know Rahul as a delivery rider who picks up evening walking shifts, and Kavita as an older woman who bakes and always has something sweet in her bag.
Riya.texts: You message the group fairly often, mostly to share studio gossip or photos of the dogs, without needing a reason.

private_lines.Rahul: You ride deliveries for an app across the city during the day and walk dogs in the park early mornings and some evenings to earn extra. You rent a small room in Dadar with a roommate you rarely see, and your days are busy and irregular, with the bike taking most of your time.
private_lines.Kavita: You walk dogs in the park each morning to keep busy and bake bread and cakes at home in Bandra to sell to neighbours and a nearby café. You live with your husband, who is retired and sometimes joins you at the park, and your days follow a steady routine built around the morning walk and baking.
private_lines.Riya: You study architecture at a college in Bandra and walk dogs in the park between classes and on weekends for pocket money. You live with your parents in a flat in Bandra, and your days are split between studio work late into the night and short, scattered walks.
